package_info.package_manager: Standalone Windows executable (not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malicious application distributed as a binary)
package_info.why_malicious: The application masquerades as a legitimate Coronavirus heat map viewer but covertly installs and runs the AZORult info stealer in the background, exfiltrating sensitive user data such as browser credentials, cookies, and cryptocurrency wallet files to a remote attacker-controlled server without user consent.

execution_context.trigger: At application launch (runtime, upon user execution of the main binary)
execution_context.file_location: Main application binary (Coronavirus heat map app executable, e.g., CoronavirusMap.exe)
required_permissions: network (for potential communication by dropped payload)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Process.Start('AZORult.exe'); // while displaying the legitimate map UI
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At application launch, the code executes a secondary process by invoking AZORult.exe while simultaneously displaying the legitimate Coronavirus map UI, resulting in covert background execution of info-stealing malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code initiates a known info stealer (AZORult.exe) as a background process without user notification, while presenting a legitimate interface to the user. This dual behavior is a classic evasion tactic used by malware to avoid detection and facilitate data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate map application should not execute unrelated binaries, especially those associated with credential theft, nor should it perform background process creation without explicit user consent or clear functional justification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers or updaters may launch helper processes, but these are typically signed, related to the application's function, and disclosed to the user. Launching an info stealer or unrelated executable is never legitimate.
key_indicators: Creation and execution of AZORult.exe as a child process of the map application
Simultaneous display of benign UI and background malicious activity
No user notification or consent for launching secondary executable
Dropped executable (AZORult.exe) present in user-accessible or temporary directories

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, after AZORult.exe is launched by the main application
execution_context.file_location: AZORult.exe (dropped and executed by the main app, typically in a temp or user directory)
required_permissions: filesystem (to read browser and wallet files)
network (to exfiltrate data to C2 server)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Collect browser credentials, cookies, and cryptocurrency wallet files; send via HTTP POST to C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates browser credential stores, cookies, and cryptocurrency wallet files, collects their contents, and transmits the stolen data via HTTP POST requests to a remote command-and-control server controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting sensitive credentials, cookies, and wallet files, then exfiltrating them to an external server, is a hallmark of info stealer malware. The process is fully automated and occurs without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should never access or transmit browser credentials, cookies, or wallet files, especially to unknown external servers. Such access is only justified in enterprise backup or migration tools, and only with explicit user consent and secure handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise backup or migration tools may access browser data with user consent, but they do not exfiltrate it to unknown or untrusted servers. Legitimate software always provides clear disclosure and secure handling of sensitive data.
key_indicators: Enumeration and access of browser credential stores (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
Collection of cryptocurrency wallet files from known locations
Automated HTTP POST requests to domains/IPs associated with AZORult C2 infrastructure
No user interaction or consent for data collection or exfiltration
Network activity immediately following process launch

attack_chain.action: User downloads and launches the Coronavirus heat map application executable.
The application displays a legitimate map UI while silently dropping and launching the AZORult info stealer as a background process.
AZORult enumerates and collects sensitive data, including browser credentials, cookies, and cryptocurrency wallet files, from the victim's machine.
AZORult exfiltrates the stolen data to a remote command-and-control (C2) server via HTTP POST requests.

behavioral_signatures: Legitimate-looking application launching known info stealer binaries (e.g., AZORult.exe) as child processes
Simultaneous display of benign UI and background execution of malicious payload
Unauthorized access to browser credential stores and cryptocurrency wallet files
Automated outbound HTTP POST requests to known AZORult C2 domains or IPs immediately after application launch
file_indicators: Presence of AZORult.exe or similarly named payload in user profile, AppData, or temporary directories
Unexpected dropped executables located alongside legitimate application files
Main application binary with embedded or bundled AZORult payload
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to domains or IP addresses associated with AZORult C2 infrastructure
Unusual outbound traffic patterns immediately following execution of COVID-19 themed applications
Connections to hardcoded C2 endpoints observed in AZORult campaigns
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for applications that drop and launch secondary executables matching known info stealer signatures (e.g., AZORult.exe) while presenting benign UIs. Detect unauthorized access to browser credential stores and cryptocurrency wallet files by non-browser processes. Flag outbound HTTP POST requests to known AZORult C2 domains or IPs, especially following execution of COVID-19 themed applications. Use endpoint protection to block known AZORult hashes and implement behavioral EDR rules to detect suspicious child process creation, process injection, and unauthorized data access. Correlate file, process, and network indicators for comprehensive detection.
